## Traditional Workflow

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {'themeVariables': {'fontSize': '28px'}}}%%

flowchart LR

A1[Code] --> F1[Figure] 
A1 --> F2["Statistical<br />result"] 
F1 --> |"Insert"| W1["Word Document"] 
F2 --> |"Copy and paste"| W1 
W1 --> P3["Publication"]
```

::: notes
What happens when the user starts from the published document and wants to go back to the analysis?
:::

## Reproducible Workflow

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {'themeVariables': {'fontSize': '28px'}}}%%

flowchart LR

C[Code] --> F[Figure]
C --> R[Résultat<br />statistique]


F <-->|"intégré"| Q[Document Quarto]
C <-->|"intégré"| Q
R <-->|"intégré"| Q

Q --> PDF[PDF]
Q --> WORD[Word]
Q --> HTML[HTML]
Q --> S[Diapositives]
```

Conceptualized by @gentleman2007

::: notes
Reader:

- can trace how each figure was generated and

- experiment with changes to the analysis in the final product.

Benefits for the author:

- easy to modify or correct the code without having to re-edit everything in the final document;

- reduces the risk of copy-and-paste errors;

- allows for more thorough revision
:::

## Word vs. Quarto

:::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Word

\+ as-is

\+ easy to use and accept revisions

\- no data traceability

\- manual work by default

\- difficult to handle large documents

\- compatibility issues

\- controlled by a single company

\
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Quarto

—two files: source +

output—learning curve for collaboration

\+ option: code vs. manual work

\+ simple yet powerful

\+ very lightweight source file

\+ free software
:::
::::


## Under the hood of Quarto

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {'themeVariables': {'fontSize': '24px'}}}%%

flowchart LR

M["Prose in<br />Markdown<br />format"]
C[Code]

M --> Q["Quarto<br />doc."]
C --> Q

Q --> K["knitr / Jupyter<br />(code execution)"]

K --> P[Pandoc]

P --> PDF[PDF]
P --> HTML[HTML]
P --> DOCX[Word]

```

## Markdown - the basics

::::::: columns
::: {.column width="40%"}

Markdown source

```         
# Title or Heading 1

## Heading 2  

Text can contain **bold** and *italics*. It can also contain `monospace formatted text`, ideal for sharing code.

- Item 1^with superscript^ 
- Item 2~with subscript~

[Hyperlink text](https://example.com) 
```
:::

::::: {.column width="60%"}

Renders as:

```{=html}
<style>
.fake-h1 { font-size: 1.6em; font-weight: 700; margin: 0.3em 0; }
.fake-h2 { font-size: 1.2em; font-weight: 600; margin: 0.3em 0; }
</style>
```

::: fake-h1
Title or Heading 1
:::

::: fake-h2
Heading 2
:::

Text can contain **bold** and *italics*. It can also contain `monospace formatted text`, ideal for sharing code.

- Item 1^with superscript^ 
- Item 2~with subscript~

[Hyperlink text](https://example.com) 
:::::
:::::::


## Markdown - Including Images

```         
![Figure caption](https://imgs.xkcd.com/comics/self_description.png)
```

Renders as:

![Figure caption](https://imgs.xkcd.com/comics/self_description.png)

## Markdown - Include tables

```         
| Tables   |     Are      |   Cool |
|----------|:------------:|-------:|
| col 1 is | on the left  |  $1600 |
| col 2 is |   centered   |    $12 |
| col 3 is | on the right |     $1 |
```
Renders as:

| Tables   |     Are      |   Cool |
|----------|:------------:|-------:|
| col 1 is | on the left  | \$1600 |
| col 2 is |   centered   |   \$12 |
| col 3 is | on the right |    \$1 |

## Markdown - Equations using Latex math

Display style:

```
$$
N_t = N_0 e^{a*t}
$$
```

Renders as:

$$
N_t = N_0 e^{a*t}
$$

Or inline: `$N_0=1$` renders as $N_0=1$

## Code to edit the document itself {.scrollable}

![](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMTk1NDgyMDk1NV5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTcwNjE3OTEwOQ@@._V1_QL75_UX500_CR0,47,500,281_.jpg){width="382"}

- Knitr
- [Filters and Extensions](https://quarto.org/docs/extensions/listing-filters.html)
- `knitr::hooks` Example:

```         
# Automatic formatting

local({
  hook_old <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("document")  
  knitr::knit_hooks$set(document = function(x) {
    x = gsub("CO2",  "CO~2~",     x, fixed=T)
    x = gsub("HCO3", "HCO~3~^-^", x, fixed=T)
    x = gsub(" um", " μm", x, fixed=T)
    x = gsub("umol", "μmol", x, fixed=T)
    x = gsub("chlorophyll a", "chlorophyll *a*", x, fixed=T)
    hook_old(x)
  })
})
```

## Git Mechanism

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"themeVariables": {"fontSize": "30px"}}}%%

flowchart LR

    GH["☁️ GitHub<br>Remote repo"]

    subgraph PC["Local computer"]
        WD["Working directory"]
        ST["Staging area<br>(git add)"]
        REPO["Local repo"]

        WD -->|"git add"| ST
        ST -->|"git commit"| REPO
    end

    GH -->|"git clone"| REPO
    REPO -->|"git push"| GH
    GH -->|"git pull"| REPO
    
style PC fill:#f8f9fa,stroke:#666,stroke-width:2px
```

Each `commit` becomes a savepoint.
